heading: Engine create and destroy
text:
### Engine create and destroy [IRET.18.1]

`ds_rete_engine_create` initialises subsystems in this order:

1. String intern table — an open-addressing hash set with
   tombstone deletion ([IRET.1.4]): pinned structural strings
   interned at load and never freed, counted `String`/`Bytes`
   slot values individually allocated and reclaimed on
   last-holder retract. All subsequent intern calls land here.
2. Schema registry — name→`ds_rete_schema_t *` map plus the
   flat schema-ID → alpha-node-list array. Empty until
   the load ([IRET.18.2]) populates it.
3. Agenda — empty binary heap.
4. TMS dependency table — empty map keyed by the justifying
   activation's timetag ([IRET.12.4]).
5. Builtin table — the global op-indexed table ([IRET.13.1]);
   the module register functions populate it, idempotently,
   before any load. See [IRET.13.2].
6. Clock — two function pointers sharing one context, the
   monotonic clock and the wall clock ([IRET.14]), defaulting
   to `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` and
   `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`.
7. Fire hooks — `before_fire` and `after_fire` pointers,
   initialised to NULL (no-op).

`ds_rete_engine_destroy` runs teardown in reverse order.
Any in-flight tokens and activations are freed; all
interned strings are released with the intern-table slab;
schema descriptors, node graphs, and expression trees are
freed.

On mid-init failure, `ds_rete_engine_create` frees every
subsystem that successfully initialised before returning the
error — no partial engine is returned to the caller.
